SL-000010.transcript:
Member (Olivia Kim): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Olivia Kim, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Kim): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Olivia Kim): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): When did you go off work?
Member (Olivia Kim): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Olivia Kim): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Olivia Kim): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Olivia Kim): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Olivia Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Olivia Kim): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Olivia Kim): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Olivia Kim): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Olivia Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.
SL-000010.narrative_summary: Olivia Kim, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a disability claim status case. Agent Sophie Belanger reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list. In the end, it was not resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

SL-000033.transcript:
Member (Leila Morrison): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Leila Morrison, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Morrison): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Leila Morrison): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Leila Morrison): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Leila Morrison): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Leila Morrison): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Leila Morrison): Yes, here in town.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Leila Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Orthodontics isn't part of your employer's plan. I can send you the booklet section, and your plan administrator at work can confirm whether that's changing.
Member (Leila Morrison): That's disappointing.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I understand. Some employers offer a health spending account that can be used for orthodontics.
Member (Leila Morrison): How would I check that?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): It would show under Accounts in the app. I don't see one on your certificate, but HR can confirm.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: orthodontics isn't in your employer's plan right now, and HR can tell you if that's changing.
Member (Leila Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah Fortin): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Hannah Fortin, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Fortin): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Hannah Fortin): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Hannah Fortin): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Hannah Fortin): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Hannah Fortin): Yes, here in town.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.

Member (Hannah Fortin): Great, that helps.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma Martin): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Emma Martin, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Emma Martin): The receiving institution says they never got anything.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Emma Martin): Who follows up?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.

Member (Tyler O'Brien): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Tyler O'Brien, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler O'Brien): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler O'Brien): Yes, that's right.
Member (Tyler O'Brien): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Tyler O'Brien): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Where is the money going?
Member (Tyler O'Brien): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Tyler O'Brien): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Tyler O'Brien): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Tyler O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Tyler O'Brien): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Tyler O'Brien): Who follows up?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Tyler O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Chantal Chen): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Chen): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Chantal Chen): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?

Member (Chantal Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Leila Wilson): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.

Member (Leila Wilson): The second. The first was denied in July.

Member (Leila Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Leila Wilson): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Leila Wilson): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Leila Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Cote): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Arjun Cote, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Cote): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun Cote): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Arjun Cote): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Arjun Cote): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Arjun Cote): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Arjun Cote): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Arjun Cote): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Arjun Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Arjun Cote): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Arjun Cote): Who follows up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Arjun Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Martin): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Owen Martin, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Martin): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Martin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Owen Martin): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Owen Martin): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): How old is he?
Member (Owen Martin): Fourteen.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Owen Martin): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Owen Martin): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Owen Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Owen Martin): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Owen Martin): Great, that helps.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.

Member (Gurpreet Patel): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Gurpreet Patel, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Gurpreet Patel): Yes, that's right.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Gurpreet Patel): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Gurpreet Patel): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Gurpreet Patel): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Gurpreet Patel): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Gurpreet Patel): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Liam Patel): The receiving institution says they never got anything.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Liam Patel): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Liam Patel): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Liam Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The transfer was held because the receiving institution's form wasn't signed. It came in this morning, so I've released it, and the funds will move within five business days.
Member (Liam Patel): So it's finally moving?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Liam Patel): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.

Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): How old is he?

Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): What's a pre-determination?

Member (Gurpreet Ahmed): Great, that helps.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.

Member (Liam Lavoie): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Liam Lavoie, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Lavoie): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Lavoie): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Liam Lavoie): The receiving institution says they never got anything.

Member (Liam Lavoie): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Liam Lavoie): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Liam Lavoie): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Liam Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The transfer was held because the receiving institution's form wasn't signed. It came in this morning, so I've released it, and the funds will move within five business days.
Member (Liam Lavoie): So it's finally moving?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Liam Lavoie): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Liam Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-001927.transcript:
Member (Olivia Kim): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Olivia Kim, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Kim): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Kim): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Olivia Kim): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Olivia Kim): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Olivia Kim): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): How much medication do you have left?
Member (Olivia Kim): About four days. That's why I'm calling now.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Olivia Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Olivia Kim): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Olivia Kim): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Olivia Kim): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Olivia Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Arjun Patel): My pension transfer has been sitting for months and my bank says they're waiting on you.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Arjun Patel, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Patel): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Arjun Patel): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Arjun Patel): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Where is the money going?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Arjun Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Arjun Patel): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Arjun Patel): Who follows up?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Arjun Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Gurpreet Wilson): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.

Member (Fatima Chen): I'm following up again — my life insurance premium tripled and nobody warned me.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: the new rate follows the renewal schedule, I've sent you the notice and a lower-coverage option, and you can decide within 30 days.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Lucas Campbell, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas Campbell): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Lucas Campbell): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Lucas Campbell): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Lucas Campbell): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Lucas Campbell): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Lucas Campbell): Yes, here in town.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontics isn't part of your employer's plan. I can send you the booklet section, and your plan administrator at work can confirm whether that's changing.
Member (Lucas Campbell): That's disappointing.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I understand. Some employers offer a health spending account that can be used for orthodontics.
Member (Lucas Campbell): How would I check that?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): It would show under Accounts in the app. I don't see one on your certificate, but HR can confirm.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: orthodontics isn't in your employer's plan right now, and HR can tell you if that's changing.
Member (Lucas Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-002611.narrative_summary: Lucas Campbell, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a coverage question case. Agent Daniel Okafor checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate. This was a continuation contact on an open issue; the agent did not reference the prior contact history and responded to the request in isolation. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 3 (neutral).

Member (Leila Campbell): I'm following up again — I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Leila Campbell, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.

Member (Leila Campbell): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Leila Campbell): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): When did you go off work?
Member (Leila Campbell): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Leila Campbell): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Leila Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Leila Campbell): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Leila Campbell): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Leila Campbell): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Owen Morrison): I'm following up again — my Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Owen Morrison, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Morrison): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Owen Morrison): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Owen Morrison): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Owen Morrison): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Owen Morrison): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Owen Morrison): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Owen Morrison): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Owen Morrison): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Owen Morrison): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Owen Morrison): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
SL-002729.narrative_summary: Owen Morrison, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a CDCP pre-authorization case. Member (Chantal Wilson): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Chantal Wilson): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Happy to check that for you.

SL-003006.transcript:
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I'm following up again — my disability payments have stopped and I have no income coming in.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Mathieu Fortin, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I was told a voicemail was left, but I never got one.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): My doctor charges for the form and I don't know which form you actually need.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Have you received any letter or message from us about your file?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Nothing in the mail. The app says 'pending information' but doesn't say what information.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Do you know who your case manager is?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): I spoke to someone once in the spring, but I don't have a name or a direct number.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): When is your next appointment with your doctor?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Next Tuesday. I can ask them then, but I need to know exactly what to ask for.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Is anyone else helping you with the claim, like your employer or a union rep?
Member (Mathieu Fortin): My HR person said it's between me and Sun Life now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file, the case manager's notes and the outstanding information request.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I can see the file. Your payments were paused on the 28th because an updated attending physician statement was due for the next review period.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The request went out as a voicemail and a message in your secure mailbox, which is why you didn't see a letter.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The file shows an attending physician statement is outstanding, and payments stay on hold until the case manager receives it. I've asked her to call you, but I can't release the payment from here.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): So I'm just supposed to go without income until then?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I know this is really hard. I've marked the file urgent so the case manager reviews the form the same day it arrives.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): Can someone at least call me when it's received?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes. Your mobile is now the preferred contact, and a call is requested for the day the form arrives.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the attending physician statement is outstanding, your case manager is calling you, and the payment is held until the form arrives.
Member (Mathieu Fortin): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
